title: Music for the moment
narration: Hello. This is MAMRS, the Mood and Action Based Music Recommendation System. It helps a listener discover songs for a particular moment, using their mood, activity, and saved music preferences. This demonstration uses a separate test account and the real application interface.

title: Two implemented core modules
notes: Accounts and saved mixes support both
narration: The two core modules demonstrated here are contextual song recommendation, and ratings and feedback. In the design mapping, the first connects UserPreference, Mood, Activity, Song, RecommendationEngine, and Recommendation. The second connects the user and song to Rating and Feedback, which influence later recommendations.

title: Save your music preferences
narration: First, I save Bollywood as a preferred genre, Arijit Singh as a preferred artist, and Hindi as the language. The application stores these choices for this account. The required language option keeps Hindi as a constraint, while artist and genre matches help prioritize suitable songs.

title: Choose a mood and activity
narration: Next, I select Romantic as the mood and Driving as the activity, then request recommendations. The server loads my preferences, available songs, and previous ratings. The recommendation engine checks the selected context tags and required preferences before ranking the eligible songs.

title: Inspect the ranked results
narration: The result shows Tum Hi Ho at the top, followed by other eligible songs. Tracks matching more preference categories take priority, and ranking points order tracks with the same match count. Only three songs qualify in this small demo catalog, so the application explains the smaller result set.

title: Understand why a song appears
narration: Opening Why this track shows the reasons behind the recommendation, including context tags and preferred artist, genre, or language. The score combines these signals with rating history and helpful feedback. These are deterministic ranking points. They are not probabilities or predictions from a trained machine learning model.

title: Submit a rating and feedback
narration: Now I rate Tum Hi Ho five out of five and mark the recommendation as helpful. I can also leave a comment. The server validates the rating and checks that this account previously received the song as a recommendation before saving the feedback.

title: See the feedback loop work
narration: The recommendations refresh after submission. In this captured run, Tum Hi Ho increases from eighty six to ninety two points, with the same context and preferences. Personal feedback changes the scoring components. The configured weights remain fixed, and free text comments are stored without sentiment analysis.

title: Keep a recommendation snapshot
narration: I can save the current recommendations as a named mix, such as Romantic drive, and open it again from Saved mixes. This supporting feature preserves a song list for later reference. The current project focuses on music discovery and recommendations; it does not stream or download songs.

title: Revisit recent moments
narration: Recent moments keeps a history of recommendation sessions. Behind the interface, the application stores the user, selected context, timestamp, and recommendation result. This connects the visible user journey to the sequence flow: request recommendations, retrieve data, calculate results, save the event, and display songs.

title: Grow a cleaner song catalog
notes: Missing labels require evidence or review
narration: Your catalog supports artist discovery through MusicBrainz and Discogs. The new command line ingestion pipeline adds persistent jobs, validation, deduplication, enrichment, and review before publication. Missing context labels remain unclassified unless evidence or review supplies them. Importing metadata alone does not establish a song's mood.

title: What the prototype demonstrates
notes: Broader catalog and label review next
No claim of complete Spotify coverage
narration: This prototype demonstrates an end to end recommendation and feedback loop, supported by preferences, history, and saved mixes. Forty automated tests pass, and the browser walkthrough verifies the score change. Next steps are broader catalog coverage, reviewed labels, and relevance evaluation. Complete Spotify coverage is not implemented. Thank you.
